record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Assuming the previous existence question has a positive answer, can one define and classify an F-type singularity of a Nijenhuis operator by requiring that, near the point, the Nijenhuis algebra Nij_L contains a gl-regular Nijenhuis operator L with Lie_e L = 0 and cyclic unity e, and that the local algebra structure is given by the construction described in §3.1.3?

evidence.quote: (2) If the answer to the previous question is affirmative, then we can define an F-type singularity of a Nijenhuis operator as follows: in a neighbourhood of such a point, NijL contains a Nijenhuis operator, which satisfies LeL = 0 ..., it is gl-regular and e is cyclic for this operator. Moreover, the structure of the algebra in a neighbourhood of this point is given by the above construction

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $L\colon TM\to TM$ a Nijenhuis operator, i.e. a (1,1)-tensor field whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)=L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically. Denote by $\mathrm{Nij}_L$ the Nijenhuis algebra associated with $L$, that is, the commutative associative algebra of (1,1)-tensors generated (pointwise and functorially) by $L$ and consisting of Nijenhuis operators commuting with $L$ in the appropriate Nijenhuis sense. A Nijenhuis operator $L$ is called gl-regular at a point $p\in M$ if at $p$ every eigenvalue of $L$ has geometric multiplicity one (equivalently, the minimal and characteristic polynomials of $L_p$ coincide). A vector field $e$ on $M$ is called a unity for $L$ if $L_e L=0$, where $L_e$ denotes the Lie derivative along $e$; the unity $e$ is called cyclic for $L$ at $p$ if the vectors $e_p,L_p e_p,\dots,L_p^{n-1}e_p$ form a basis of $T_pM$ (with $n=\dim M$).

Consider the following local algebraic construction at a point $p\in M$: take a gl-regular Nijenhuis operator $\widetilde L\in \mathrm{Nij}_L$ defined in a neighbourhood of $p$ satisfying $L_e\widetilde L=0$ and with $e$ cyclic for $\widetilde L$; declare the algebra structure in this neighbourhood to be that generated by $\widetilde L$ on the cyclic frame $\{e,\widetilde L e,\dots,\widetilde L^{n-1}e\}$.

Assume that the prior existence question — whether such a gl-regular operator $\widetilde L\in\mathrm{Nij}_L$ with cyclic unity $e$ satisfying $L_e\widetilde L=0$ exists in a neighbourhood of any candidate F-type singular point — has an affirmative answer.

Problem: Define an F-type singularity of the Nijenhuis operator $L$ at $p$ to be a point at which the above conditions hold (existence in a neighbourhood of $p$ of $\widetilde L\in \mathrm{Nij}_L$ that is gl-regular, with $L_e\widetilde L=0$ and $e$ cyclic for $\widetilde L$, and with the local algebra structure given by the construction above). Determine whether this definition is well-posed, intrinsic, and independent of the choices involved, and classify all F-type singularities of Nijenhuis operators in this sense, providing normal forms.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (Antonov–Konyaev–Matveev and related) study gl-regular Nijenhuis operators with a unity and identify regular F-manifolds with Nijenhuis manifolds with a cyclic unity, and produce seminormal forms in dimensions 2 and 3 near singularities. A full definition and classification of F-type singularities of Nijenhuis operators in arbitrary dimension, as formulated here, has not been established in the literature found; the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis operators with a unity and F-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes gl-regular Nijenhuis operators with a unity around algebraically generic points and gives seminormal forms in dimensions 2 and 3.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification exists in low dimensions but general F-type singularity classification is not completed.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of two-dimensional Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Normal forms of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators near singular points in dimension two are obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity classification is so far only completed in low dimension.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies gl-regular Nijenhuis operators and their local description via companion forms.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the gl-regular framework underlying the proposed F-type definition.
